subject: medicine
title: Neurological localisation and cranial nerves: key high-yield principles

steps.tx: Localisation starts with asking whether the lesion is **upper motor neuron** or **lower motor neuron**. UMN lesions cause spasticity, brisk reflexes, clonus and an extensor plantar (**Babinski sign**). LMN lesions cause flaccidity, reduced reflexes, wasting and fasciculations. Pronator drift points to a corticospinal lesion.
steps.say: Localisation starts with asking whether the lesion is upper motor neuron or lower motor neuron. Upper motor neuron lesions cause spasticity, brisk reflexes, clonus and an extensor plantar response, called the Babinski sign. Lower motor neuron lesions cause flaccidity, reduced reflexes, wasting and fasciculations. Pronator drift points to a corticospinal lesion.

steps.tx: **Lateral medullary syndrome**, or **Wallenberg syndrome**, follows occlusion of the posterior inferior cerebellar artery. It gives ipsilateral facial pain and temperature loss, ipsilateral Horner features, dysphagia, hoarseness, vertigo and ataxia, with contralateral body pain and temperature loss. Posterior column sensation is spared.
steps.say: Lateral medullary syndrome, also called Wallenberg syndrome, follows occlusion of the posterior inferior cerebellar artery. It gives ipsilateral facial pain and temperature loss, ipsilateral Horner features, dysphagia, hoarseness, vertigo and ataxia. Pain and temperature loss on the opposite side of the body occurs, while posterior column sensation is spared.

steps.tx: **Third nerve palsy** causes a down and out eye, ptosis and a dilated pupil. A pupil-involving palsy is a compressive lesion until proven otherwise. **Horner syndrome** gives miosis, partial ptosis and anhidrosis, with the pupil still reacting to light. Apparent enophthalmos is not true enophthalmos.
steps.say: Third nerve palsy causes a down and out eye, ptosis and a dilated pupil. A pupil-involving palsy is treated as a compressive lesion until proven otherwise. Horner syndrome gives miosis, partial ptosis and anhidrosis, with the pupil still reacting to light. The sunken look is apparent, not true enophthalmos.

steps.tx: **Bell palsy** is an acute lower motor neuron seventh nerve palsy affecting the whole face on one side, including the forehead. **Trigeminal neuralgia** causes brief, electric, unilateral pain in a trigeminal division, triggered by chewing or touch, with a normal examination between attacks. The maxillary division is most often involved. Carbamazepine is first line.

steps.tx: Cortical localisation matters for speech. A lesion in the **inferior frontal gyrus** (Broca area) causes motor aphasia with preserved comprehension. A lesion of the **arcuate fasciculus** causes conduction aphasia, with fluent speech, impaired repetition and intact comprehension. **Gerstmann syndrome** combines dysgraphia, dyscalculia, finger agnosia and left-right confusion from a dominant parietal lesion.
steps.say: Cortical localisation matters for speech. A lesion in the inferior frontal gyrus, Broca area, causes motor aphasia with preserved comprehension. A lesion of the arcuate fasciculus causes conduction aphasia, with fluent speech, impaired repetition and intact comprehension. Gerstmann syndrome combines dysgraphia, dyscalculia, finger agnosia and left-right confusion from a dominant parietal lesion.

steps.tx: Internuclear ophthalmoplegia results from a lesion of the **medial longitudinal fasciculus**, giving impaired adduction in the affected eye with nystagmus in the abducting eye. In exam questions, remember that naming is preserved in pure word blindness and pure word deafness, and that vibration sense is the sense most often lost with age.
